Description:
As a reader I want to search the catalogue so that I find a book fast.

Acceptance criteria:
1. The search box is on the catalogue page and has the label "Search books".
2. Search matches title and author, ignoring upper and lower case.
3. Results update while typing, after a short pause.
4. If nothing matches, the page shows "No books found" and a "Clear search" link.
5. An empty search shows all books.
6. Search text longer than 100 characters is cut to 100 characters.

Notes: API: `GET /api/books?q=` (see `openapi/bookshelf.openapi.yaml`).

Summary: BS-102 Add to cart with quantity
Description:
As a reader I want to choose how many copies I buy.

Acceptance criteria:
1. On the book page the quantity field accepts whole numbers from 1 to 10. Default is 1.
2. Values outside 1-10, decimals and empty values are rejected with the message "Choose from 1 to 10 copies".
3. After "Add to cart" the page shows "Added to cart" and the cart badge shows the new number of books.
4. Adding the same book again increases its quantity; the total for one book can never exceed 10.
5. The same rules apply to the API (`POST /api/cart/items`, `PATCH /api/cart/items/{bookId}`).

Notes: The cart badge is the number next to "Cart" in the header.

As a reader I want free delivery on bigger orders.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Standard delivery costs 4.90 EUR.
2. Standard delivery is free when the subtotal after discount is 30.00 EUR or more.
3. Pickup point delivery is always free.
4. The cart shows "Free delivery" or "Delivery: 4.90 EUR" next to the total.
5. Below 30.00 EUR the cart shows "Add X EUR more for free delivery", where X is the missing amount.

Notes: Book prices are in `data/books.json`. Money is calculated in cents.

As a reader I want to enter my delivery details and place the order.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Fields: full name (2-80 chars), email, street, city, postcode (3-10 chars), delivery option. All are required.
2. Invalid fields show an error text next to the field when the reader leaves the field and on "Place order".
3. The form meets WCAG 2.2 level AA: every field has a visible label, errors are announced as text, the whole form works with the keyboard.
4. "Place order" creates exactly one order and opens the order page.
5. After a successful order the cart is empty.

Notes: Page: `/checkout`. API: `POST /api/orders`.

The shop should support Ukrainian properly. Customers from Ukraine should feel at home.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Ukrainian is available.
2. Texts look correct.

Notes: Translations are in `public/i18n/uk.json`.

As a reader I want to use promo codes from newsletters.

Acceptance criteria:
1. A reader can apply one promo code per order.
2. `WELCOME10` gives 10% off the subtotal.
3. `BOOKS5` gives 5.00 EUR off when the subtotal is 25.00 EUR or more.
4. `WELCOME10` can be combined with any other promo code.
5. Free delivery is calculated from the subtotal before the discount.

Notes: Marketing wants the free-delivery message to "always match the total the reader pays".

As a signed-in reader I want to see my orders.

Acceptance criteria:
1. `GET /api/orders` returns only the orders of the signed-in user.
2. `GET /api/orders/{orderId}` returns the order only if it belongs to the signed-in user. For any other order it returns 404, the same as for an order that does not exist.
3. Without a valid token both endpoints return 401.
4. Guests can place orders but `GET /api/orders` returns an empty list for a new guest session.

Notes: Demo users: `reader.one@example.com` and `reader.two@example.com`. The password is `DEMO_PASSWORD` from your `.env` file.

Checkout should be fast and not annoying. Users complained that it feels slow.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Checkout is fast.
2. No double orders.
